events.label:
Leonardo's drawings
in the Codex Madrid I
events.note: An important precursor: in the manuscripts of the Codex Madrid I, Leonardo records observations on mechanics and strength, but does not yet arrive at a complete theory of beams. The codex was found in the Biblioteca Nacional in Madrid in 1965; the discovery was announced in 1967.

events.label: Columbus reaches America
events.note: External chronological reference, included only as a time anchor to show how old the earliest studies in mechanics are.

events.label:
Galileo:
Two New Sciences
events.note: In the "Discorsi e dimostrazioni matematiche intorno a due nuove scienze", printed in Leiden in 1638, Galileo studies the strength of rods and the fracture of solid bodies: one of the first steps towards a theory of bending, although still based on incorrect assumptions.

events.label:
Jakob Bernoulli:
curvature proportional to M
events.note: He assumes that the curvature of the bent bar is proportional to the bending moment. A first treatment appeared in the Acta Eruditorum in 1694; the final version is in the memoirs of the Paris Academy for 1705, the year of his death.

events.label:
Daniel Bernoulli
suggests the energy
approach to Euler
events.note: In a letter of 20 October 1742, Daniel Bernoulli suggests to Euler that the elastic curve be found by minimising the integral of the squared curvature: in today's terms, a strain energy.

events.label:
Euler: correct equation
of the elastic curve
events.note: In the appendix "De curvis elasticis" of the "Methodus inveniendi lineas curvas" (1744), Euler follows Daniel Bernoulli's suggestion, obtains the equation of the elastic curve and classifies its shapes; the same appendix contains the buckling load of a column.

events.label:
Daniel Bernoulli:
transverse vibrations
of beams
events.note: "De vibrationibus et sono laminarum elasticarum", in the Commentarii of the St Petersburg Academy, vol. 13 (for 1741-43), printed in 1751: the Bernoulli-Euler theory is applied to the transverse vibrations of bars. Bernoulli had written to Euler about the vibrating rod as early as 1735.

events.label:
Navier: correct theory
of bending
events.note: In the "Résumé des leçons données à l'École des ponts et chaussées" (1826), Navier develops the modern engineering analysis of beams, computing forces and deflections for various supports and load cases.

events.label:
de Saint-Venant:
shear effects
in bending
events.note: "Mémoire sur la flexion des prismes" (Journal de Mathématiques Pures et Appliquées, 1856): an exact solution of the equations of elasticity for a bent prism, with the shear stresses and the warping of the cross-sections. It follows the memoir on torsion, read at the Académie des Sciences in 1853 and printed in 1855, where the semi-inverse method is introduced.

events.label:
Timoshenko beam
(includes shear)
events.note: Date of the well-known paper in the Philosophical Magazine. The theory, which includes shear deformation and rotary inertia, was developed with Paul Ehrenfest in 1912-1913 and first printed in Timoshenko's Russian textbook on elasticity (1916).
